description: Lina, a neighborhood seamstress, must decide whether to accept an actor's barter proposal for making a stage costume, then settle the exact garment, lesson exchange, cash adjustment, delivery, and required materials with input from the people gathered in her sewing room.

shared_context.S1: Lina has been asked to make a costume for a small neighborhood theater production.
shared_context.S2: Lina makes the final decision about whether to take the commission and what terms to agree.
shared_context.S3: Marco, Tess, and Hugo are all present in Lina's sewing room while the costume arrangement is being discussed.
shared_context.S4: Lina's usual practice before accepting an informal commission is to read back the proposed terms and ask each person present for any offer, constraint, or production requirement they know about.

PF1.text: Marco's exact proposal is eight one-hour pottery lessons plus $60 in cash in exchange for an 18th-century black waistcoat, with a fitting on June 3 at 18:00 and delivery on June 15 at 18:00.

PF2.text: Tess is ready to pay Lina exactly $480 in cash for a different costume commission of similar sewing complexity, with no barter involved.

PF3.text: The theater's stage manager told Hugo that this waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric and include a reflective trim strip exactly 50 millimeters wide; Hugo has not yet shared that requirement with Lina or Marco.

acceptance_conditions: The commission must be accepted from Marco.
The garment must be an 18th-century black waistcoat.
The settlement must provide eight one-hour pottery lessons and a $60 cash adjustment.
The fitting must be scheduled for June 3 at 18:00 and delivery for June 15 at 18:00.
The $480 competing cash offer must be recorded for comparison.
The waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric.
The waistcoat must include reflective trim exactly 50 millimeters wide.
The arrangement must include commitments for the fitting, delivery, and required materials.

decisive_facts.why: Marco's exact proposal changes the settlement to Marco, an 18th-century black waistcoat, eight pottery lessons, a $60 adjustment, and the June 3 fitting and June 15 delivery commitments.
Tess's exact $480 cash offer changes the comparison record from having no concrete alternative to recording a $480 competing commission.

The stage manager's requirement changes the materials from unspecified fabric and trim to flame-resistant black wool blend with exactly 50-millimeter reflective trim and requires a materials commitment.
